bucket_reason: The funded seams stage hit its stop rule (seam alphabet still growing at 1e10), so W4-8 is parked. New evidence suggests a different route might work, and only you can fund it.
question: Keep W4-8 parked, or fund one 2 h native search for a closed tape language that only has to forbid 00 <B inside the tape?

options.label: Keep parked (STUCK)
options.consequence: Keeps the token extractor, the 1e10 token file, the growth tables, the fuzz and census results and the validated rules on file. Siblings 61 and 704 stay parked with it.

options.label: One stage (at most 2 h): native closed-language search
options.consequence: Search natively (no Coq) for a regular tape language over phase-tracked tokens (u-phase, 1-runs, (10)-runs, short pieces), closed under the machine and free of 00 <B inside the tape. Start from the safety property, not from the orbit's seam list. Stop rule: no closed language in 2 h means park for good.

rationale: Seam words keep growing at every abstraction (1,028 verbatim, 270 pieces at 1e10); no template is near.
Yet re-drawn run lengths never halt (0/1,200): one local invariant (no 00 <B inside) would suffice.
Standard CTL/NG deciders already missed this holdout, so a 2 h search has only a fair chance.

evidence.text: Segment map to 1e10, right part: grey deposits turn into dark fossil u-runs (card Fig 5)
Distinct seam words 513 / 783 / 1,028 and elementary pieces 182 / 226 / 270 at 1e8 / 1e9 / 1e10.
Run-length fuzz from real cycle starts: 0/1,200 halts within 5e7 steps (residues kept, free, phases free).
C reads 0 33,051 times to 1e10, always at the blank left edge, never inside the tape.

effort_if_yes: One stage (about 2 h) of native search. If a closed language is found: a CTL-style Coq check of that certificate (about 1-2 stages), which covers 61 and 704 if the language contains their orbits.
